tob-4059: The second volume of Isis Unveiled turns from science to church teaching, charging that priests warped a pure first wisdom shared by all faiths. Blavatsky sets Christian tenets beside Hindu, Buddhist, and Egyptian sources to argue it. The book made her the most hotly debated faith-writer of her time.
tob-4159: Jung’s breakaway book reads a young woman’s daydreams as the hidden mind dreaming in myth. Where Freud saw only buried cravings, Jung found the old gods and heroes alive in us still. Beatrice Hinkle’s rendering bore this founding text of mind-doctoring to English readers.
tob-0159: Steiner’s Freedom-philosophy holds free will a truth — and clear self-steered thinking a holy deed. Penned in 1894 ere his Anthroposophy, it is his most close-reasoned think-book. The work bridges German high-thought and his later wonder-lore.
tob-4259: Henrik Ibsen’s Peer Gynt — 1867 — is the great Norse play-poem, dogging the braggart Peer from firth to waste and home again. The Archers’ Englishing bore it to our readers. Its trolls and Button-Moulder are world-famed. A cornerstone of latter-day playcraft.
cia-0000102959: From June 1987, this declassified report maps prison work camps in Karaganda Oblast, a region of Soviet Kazakhstan. It records camp locations and details the CIA could gather on the forced-labor network deep inside the USSR. Documents like this one helped American analysts estimate the size and reach of the Soviet prison system during the 1980s.
cia-0000109059: Bolsheviks and Heroes: The USSR and Cuba, dated October 1967 — a study of how Moscow and Havana used revolutionary mythology to cement their bond. Shared heroes and shared ideology papered over real disagreements. The report shows analysts reading propaganda as politics, looking for the cracks beneath the slogans.
cia-0000126859: An April 1966 memo to the White House about Ramparts magazine — subject deleted. Ramparts had exposed CIA funding of student and labor groups, sparking a scandal. The censored subject guards the specifics, but the context is clear: the agency's secret empire, springing leaks.
cia-0000126959: A November 1965 country report simply titled Venezuela. Oil-rich, democratic, and fighting a leftist insurgency, Venezuela was the hemisphere's success story under strain. The document is the whole country in a file — Washington's Venezuela, distilled.
cia-0000132159: Situation Report 476 on Iraq-Kuwait: Iraq widening its reserve call-up as France joined the coalition's Desert phase — the truncated title hints at the rest. Both sides were mobilizing for the ground war. The document captures the final arming before the storm broke.
cia-0000132659: A November 1960 report: Communist China concluding an aid pact with Cuba and agreeing to increase trade. Beijing's checkbook joined Moscow's. The document is the pact: the aid, promised; the trade, expanded.
cia-0000132759: A 1960 report: Cuba continuing to tighten its Soviet bloc ties. The embrace kept tightening — each month, closer. The document is the knot, pulled tight: the alliance, hardening.
cia-0000135859: A 1952 record of a conference with a deleted participant. The early plotting, behind closed doors. The entry is the meeting: the conspiracy, conferring.
cia-0000136159: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for PRINCEP on transmitting messages verbatim — and for ONTRICH, the truncated title suggests more. Word-for-word mattered. The entry is the instruction: the messages, exact.
cia-0000136259: A 1954 Guatemalan press digest for June 15 through 17. The invasion's eve, in newsprint. The document is the digest: the press, condensed — the storm, coming.
cia-0000136359: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN transmitting messages 17, 18, and 19 received from somewhere — the truncated title cuts off the source. The numbered relays. The entry is the transmission: the messages, forwarded.
cia-0000136959: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN requesting preparations in the event of PAGE-something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The contingency, readied. The document is the preparation: the event, anticipated.
cia-0000141159: A 1961 cable on ETA and reservations information for a security officer and associates — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The travel, arranged. The document is the booking: the officer, accommodated.
un-ga-res-2159: Resolution 2159 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1966. The sixties Assembly at work. The number and year survive; the decision belongs to the text.
un-ga-res-a-69-59: General Assembly Resolution A/69/59, adopted in 2014. The session's business continued. The entry is the record: the designation, the year — the rest, the text's.
un-sc-res-359: Security Council Resolution 359, adopted in 1974. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1459: Security Council Resolution 1459, cataloged with the year 2002 — the numbering suggests 2003, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1759: Security Council Resolution 1759, adopted in 2007 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-2059: Security Council Resolution 2059, adopted in 2012 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000136559: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136559. The exiles' Spanish papers, another bundle. The document is the bundle: the papers, numbered.
cia-0000136759: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136759. The invasion year's firm-dated documents. The entry is the firmness: the year, certain.
plos-pone-0000059: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on the taxonomic reliability of DNA sequences in public sequence databases — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Are GenBank's species labels trustworthy? The paper is the audit: the labels, checked.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d59: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, October 26, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 59. The same day, the answer. The message is the swiftness: the reply, same-day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d159: A report by the Joint Strategic Survey Committee — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 159. The strategists' assessment. The report is the strategy: the committee, surveying.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d259: A Chinese summary record — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 259. China's account of the talks. The record is China's: the summary, theirs.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d359: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 359. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the narrative, carried over.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d459: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 459. The connective joint. The note is the joint: the documents, touching.
copyright-renewals-1959: This Library of Congress catalog lists the copyrights renewed across America in 1959 — books, music, plays, and films whose owners claimed another term of protection. Such records were the working tools of publishers and studios managing their libraries of rights. Today they serve historians tracing which works survived in print and which slipped away.
peregrine-s-progress-pg7059: Jeffery Farnol's hero Peregrine progresses through Regency England — high roads, old inns, duels at dawn, and ladies in distress — in the author's inimitable romantic style. Dashing, colorful, and utterly Farnol from first page to last. A swashbuckling delight for all lovers of the historical romance.
arxiv-2605-09059: AI writes code now, but how good is it really? Joanna Szych and Anne Schwerk evaluate LLM-generated code with a benchmark plus a developer study — measuring the code and asking the humans who use it. The 2026 paper grounds code-generation hype in evidence.
arxiv-2605-09159: When a model reasons, does it argue with itself — an internal polylogue of competing personas? Nils A. Herrmann, Leander Girrbach, Kirill Bykov, and colleagues investigate reasoning through the lens of personas. The 2026 paper is a philosophical-empirical probe of machine inner life.
arxiv-2605-09359: AI agents need skills that improve with practice, not fixed scripts frozen at training time. Yash Vishe, Rohan Surana, Xunyi Jiang, and colleagues evolve agent skills via reinforcement learning in Skill-R1. The 2026 paper grows agent capabilities the Darwinian way: mutate, test, keep the winners.
arxiv-2605-09559: Shock waves peel airflow off surfaces, and the separated shear layer's path to turbulence decides drag and heating. Flavio Savarino, Denis Sipp, and Georgios Rigas find the optimal non-linear mechanisms driving the transition. The 2026 paper is aerodynamics at the edge of chaos.
arxiv-2605-09859: Fine-grained image retrieval — telling sparrow species apart — benefits from generative appearance priors, properly aligned. Shijie Wang, Yadan Luo, Zijian Wang, and colleagues learn that alignment end-to-end. The 2026 paper is computer vision for the very finest visual distinctions.
arxiv-2605-09959: Open-ended generation from zero data via self-play — G-Zero. Chengsong Huang, Haolin Liu, Tong Zheng, and colleagues build the self-play system. The 2026 paper is generative AI bootstrapped from nothing. It creates something from an empty starting point, improving iteratively.
plos-pone-0003459: Occupational-health researchers checked on latex-allergic health workers in this 2008 German study. After rules pushed hospitals toward powder-free rubber gloves, the team assessed the workers' quality of life and ability to keep working. The findings measure whether that single policy change genuinely improved daily life for people sensitized to natural rubber latex.
plos-pone-0003559: Diabetes researchers traced the family tree inside a single islet in this 2008 paper. The insulin-making beta cells of one human pancreatic islet turned out to descend from multiple progenitors, not one clone. That mixed ancestry reshapes how scientists think about growing replacement beta cells for diabetes therapy.
plos-pone-0003659: In 2009, a team linked lasting stress to a brain surface protein. Rats under long-term stress changed how much M6a their brains made, a protein that sits on nerve fibers. The M6a shift adds a chemical face to how strain over weeks reshapes nerve branches and contact points.
plos-pone-0003759: A blood test for colon cancer took a step forward in this 2008 study. Grützmann, Molnar, and Pilarsky showed that methylated Septin 9 DNA in peripheral blood flags colorectal cancer with useful sensitivity. Since early detection lifts survival above 90 percent, a simple blood draw could save many lives.
plos-pone-0003859: Working in 2008, a team mapped gene-family crosstalk in the developing brain. Prdm proto-oncogene transcription factors were found interacting with the Notch-Hes pathway during neural development. The expression patterns show how these gene families cooperate to build a working nervous system.
plos-pone-0003959: In 2008, Rodriguez-Vita, Sanchez-Galan, and Santamaria tied statins' vessel effects to a signaling path. The TGF-beta/Smad pathway proved essential for statin action on vascular smooth muscle cells. The mechanism clarifies how cholesterol drugs also calm artery walls.
plos-pone-0004059: In 2008, Varani, Souza, and Nakaya traced viral ghosts inside a plant killer. Prophage-like regions shaped genome differences among Xylella fastidiosa strains. The bacterium causes grave crop diseases across the Americas. The old viral fossils mark where genomes split and shifted.
plos-pone-0004159: In 2008, Wolf, Yang, and Wang mapped the master of the lens. Pax6-dependent gene networks were fully charted in the growing mouse lens. The transcription factor switched lens-building genes on and off. The network map explains how eyes gain their clarity.
plos-pone-0004259: In 2009, Lam, Urban-Grimal, and Bugnicourt mapped a tiny yeast shipping handshake. The tag-removing enzyme Ubp2 and the tag-adding ligase Rsp5 teamed up for cargo delivery. Their teamwork proved vital for moving cargo to its dock. The yeast mechanism informs human cell biology too.
plos-pone-0004359: In 2009, Qin, Zhao, and Wang brewed plastic's key building block without sterilizing. Non-sterilized fermentation produced polymer-grade L-lactic acid from a heat-loving microbe. The skip-the-autoclave method cut costs. The process greens bioplastic making nicely. The new strain tolerates open, hot fermentation.
plos-pone-0352359: Open government data promises innovation — but who actually connects? This paper asked who gets connected, studying open data’s role in access to intercity innovation networks. The findings reveal whether open data democratizes innovation or merely helps the already-connected get further ahead.
plos-pone-0358359: Lactate — the molecule behind the exercise burn — may also signal kidney trouble in diabetes. This exploratory analysis linked serum lactate to renal dysfunction in diabetic kidney disease, integrating animal experiments with clinical cohorts. The lactate connection could become a valuable early warning for failing kidneys.
plos-pone-0357959: Brazilian cordel — beloved folk poetry chapbooks — can carry life-saving health messages. This paper developed and content-validated an educational cordel supporting self-care among pregnant women with diabetes. The culturally grounded tool speaks in a voice mothers already trust, making medical advice feel like home.
plos-pone-0357759: Copper-graphite composites for brushes and bearings need exactly the right recipe. This paper predicted the properties of sintered copper-graphite composites using response surface methodology. The statistical models guide manufacturers toward sintering conditions that produce the best-performing material.
plos-pone-0357259: Older Chinese adults juggle multiple chronic diseases — and their mental health pays the price. This study examined chronic disease multimorbidity and mental health, testing family and social support as moderators. The findings show that strong support networks genuinely buffer the psychological toll of being multiply ill.
plos-pone-0357459: Education can lift families out of poverty — but can it keep them from sliding back? This paper studied the impact and mechanisms of educational human capital on the risk of relapse into poverty, using evidence from Chinese micro-families. The findings reveal schooling’s protective power and exactly how it works.
plos-pone-0353559: Immune signatures of infection should work across different patient datasets — but often don’t. This paper tested the external transportability of bacterial- and viral-associated host-response modules across public transcriptomic cohorts. The validation reveals which gene signatures genuinely travel and which collapse outside their home dataset.
plos-pone-0357159: Diatoms settled on the seafloor may seed autumn’s phytoplankton blooms when storms resuspend them. This Chukchi Sea process study examined the effects of settled diatoms on autumn blooms via sediment resuspension. The findings link the seafloor’s memory to the surface ocean’s productivity.
plos-pone-0356759: Steep mountain gullies can unleash debris flows with terrifying speed. This paper investigated the disaster mechanisms and hazard assessment of rapid steep-gully debris flows using FLO-2D simulation. The modeled scenarios give mountain communities a scientific basis for evacuation planning and defenses.
plos-pone-0353859: ‘Just trying to make it work’ — healthcare providers’ candid words on merging mental health and HIV care. This qualitative exploration examined implementation considerations from providers integrating the two services. Their grounded insights reveal what makes integrated care survive contact with real clinics.
plos-pone-0343859: Cancer steals more than health from Ghanaian women with gynecological cancers — it steals reproductive futures. This paper explored their experiences of reproductive loss in fertility’s shadow. The intimate accounts demand that oncology care in resource-limited settings address the grief of lost motherhood, not just the tumor.
plos-pone-0355559: Influenza’s dance with weather varies across Taiwan’s regions. This paper associated meteorological factors with influenza incidence, revealing regional heterogeneity in a subtropical climate. The findings refine flu forecasting for an island where one weather model doesn’t fit all.
plos-pone-0355859: Building an artificial left ventricle powered by pneumatic muscles requires systematic design. This paper methodologically developed such a simulator using interpretive structural modeling. The structured development approach yields a test platform for cardiac devices that beats — literally — like the real thing.
plos-pone-0356059: Some gut bacteria wear sugar coats that the immune system reads. CLR-Seq is a pipeline identifying bacterial species with immune-relevant glycan moieties through human C-type lectin receptor interaction. The tool maps the glycan conversations between microbiome and immunity — a new lens on host-microbe dialogue.
plos-pone-0355959: Gas-insulated switchgear fails when stray metal particles lurk inside — and finding them is hard. This paper used distributed optical fiber sensing via frequency-swept interferometry to detect metal particle defects in GIS. The fiber-optic approach promises to catch the contaminants that trigger catastrophic electrical failures.
plos-pone-0355659: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted the paper claiming antiviral effects of the novel herbal medicine KIOM-C against diverse viruses. The notice formally withdraws those findings from the scientific record.
plos-pone-0340559: HPV vaccination in rural Kerala — students, parents, and teachers all shape uptake. This pilot feasibility study explored their perceptions and practices. The findings reveal the knowledge gaps and cultural currents that vaccination programs must navigate to protect girls from cervical cancer.
plos-pone-0355359: China’s electricity market reform demands new capabilities from power companies’ sales teams. This paper examined the triadic capabilities of sales personnel in power generation enterprises — their generation and evolution mechanisms. The findings guide human capital strategy for an industry in transition.
plos-pone-0354159: Blowing past the 1.5°C climate boundary will reshape global disease — and AI can forecast how. This paper used AI to forecast the global disease burden and health inequities beyond that planetary boundary. The projections warn that climate overshoot won’t just sicken the world — it will sicken the poor far more than the rich.
plos-pone-0355159: When a young child seizes with fever, Jordanian mothers’ home responses decide outcomes. This paper studied mothers’ home management practices during febrile seizures in children under six. The findings reveal dangerous misconceptions — and the education that could replace panic with effective action.
europmc-pmc2790859: Published in 2009, this research paper tests a drug called PD 0332991, which blocks two cell-growth switches (cyclin D kinases 4 and 6) in human breast cancer cells grown in the lab. It finds the drug works best against estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer cells, the common luminal type. The results helped build the case for this drug class as a targeted breast cancer treatment.
europmc-pmc2806359: Family trees of life built from different data can clash, leaving biologists with rival charts. This 2010 paper brings TreeGraph 2, software that folds many tree results into one clear view. The authors show how it merges and draws the data. The tool helps teams weigh rival trees instead of backing one blind.
europmc-pmc2811159: Nerve fibers stay alive for decades, and this 2010 paper identifies a protein that keeps them that way. The authors demonstrate that the body's own Nmnat2 is essential for maintaining healthy axons, the long cables nerves use to send signals. Without it, axons fall apart. The finding points to a natural protective factor against nerve degeneration.
europmc-pmc2814859: Two similar drugs, azacitidine and decitabine, are used against acute myeloid leukemia, but how do they compare head to head? This 2010 paper tests both in leukemia cell lines, measuring their activity side by side. The authors map where the drugs behave alike and where they differ. The comparison helps explain their distinct clinical profiles.
europmc-pmc2873959: Tiny RNAs shift with age, and this 2010 paper charts the drift. The authors show microRNA patterns reveal how target-gene activity changes as people grow older. Their profiles link small RNAs to the aging process itself. The work offered fresh markers of biological age that later studies could test.
europmc-pmc2898859: Mold toxins in food cause liver cancer, and this 2010 paper counts the toll. The authors assess the global burden of aflatoxin-driven liver cancer with risk math. Their count pins down a preventable killer. The numbers argue for better grain storage worldwide.
europmc-pmc2911859: Aching bodies with fibromyalgia may gain from movement. This 2010 pooled study tests types of aerobic exercise in fibromyalgia trials. The authors find moving truly eases signs like pain and fatigue. Their math gave patients a proof-backed push to move, turning exercise into a first-line prescription.
europmc-pmc2924359: The monkey AIDS virus wrecks the gut wall, this 2010 paper shows. The authors link damaged intestinal lining to microbial leakage in pathogenic SIV infections. Their work mirrors human HIV gut damage closely. The finding underscores the gut as a key battleground.
europmc-pmc2965659: Comparing brain networks of different sizes is tricky. This 2010 paper tackles comparing brain networks of different size and connectivity density using graph theory. The authors' methods level the playing field. Their work aids fair network comparisons. Size effects no longer fool the analysis.
europmc-pmc3037559: Ocean viruses got their genomes compared. This 2010 paper pits sea cyanoviruses against T4-like viruses from many hosts. The authors reveal viral diversity. Their work lights up marine ecology. Seawater teems with more viruses than stars. These viruses steer the planet's carbon cycle.
europmc-pmc3069059: Study weighting needs trimming. This 2011 paper covers trimming wild weights in propensity-score studies. The authors' guidance steadies causal claims. Their work shaped epidemiology. Extreme weights can warp the answer. Trimming trades a little bias for stability. The paper gives practical cutoffs.
europmc-pmc3087759: Twitter tracked the swine flu pandemic. This 2011 paper shows tweets mirrored H1N1 spread and public worry. The authors prove the signal is real. Their work launched digital disease tracking. Health agencies now mine the firehose. The method flagged outbreaks days early.
europmc-pmc3098059: Gene-switch maps got an annotator. This 2010 paper brings ChIPpeakAnno, a tool that labels ChIP-seq peaks. The authors' package spread through labs. Their software aided gene studies. Peak maps finally got readable labels. The tool runs inside Bioconductor. Thousands of studies cite the package.
europmc-pmc6514059: Natural killer cells are the immune system's assassins, and natural cytotoxicity receptors are the triggers that tell them to fire. This review covers NKp46, NKp44, and NKp30 - the first such receptors ever cloned - and how they recognize tumors and infections. Two decades of research show these sensors shaping cancer defense, autoimmunity, and pregnancy, making them tempting targets for new therapies.
europmc-pmc6517359: Inflammation needs brakes as well as an accelerator, and the PPAR family of proteins helps provide them. These nuclear receptors - PPAR-alpha, beta/delta, and gamma - sense fatty molecules and dial immune responses up or down. This review explains how they self-regulate inflammation, a mechanism behind existing diabetes drugs and a target for taming chronic inflammatory diseases.
europmc-pmc6518059: Empagliflozin, a diabetes drug, unexpectedly cut cardiovascular deaths in trials - but nobody knew why. This study found a clue in heart cells: the drug lowers sodium buildup inside them by blocking a sodium-hydrogen exchanger. Less intracellular sodium means a calmer, more efficient heartbeat. The mechanism helps explain how a kidney-targeted diabetes pill ended up protecting the heart.
europmc-pmc6520659: NF-kappaB is a master-switch protein that turns genes on in immunity and cancer - but its day job in the nervous system is subtler. This review examines how different brain cell types use the same switch for different ends: neurons, glia, and immune cells each wire it to their own functions. Mapping these cell-specific roles clarifies how the factor shapes learning, injury, and disease.
europmc-pmc6582859: A cut sets off a choreographed repair: first inflammation clears debris, then new tissue fills the gap, and finally remodeling strengthens the patch. This comprehensive review walks through each phase of skin wound healing and the cells and signals driving it. Understanding the choreography helps doctors nudge slow or stuck wounds toward closure.
europmc-pmc6600059: Oxidative stress - rogue oxygen molecules beating the body's defenses - harms sperm as surely as other cells. This systematic review examines how reactive oxygen species affect male fertility and what helps: testing methods, antioxidant treatments, and lifestyle fixes. The guidance helps clinicians evaluate and manage a common, missed cause of infertility.
europmc-pmc6615259: Infections can trigger depression-like behavior through brain inflammation - and melatonin may blunt it. In mice given bacterial toxin, the sleep hormone calmed overactive microglia and quieted the NLRP3 inflammasome, easing depressive-like symptoms. The study hints at an unexpected anti-inflammatory role for melatonin in mood.
europmc-pmc6667459: Mapping which proteins touch - via cross-linked peptides - needs serious computing. pLink 2 is a high-speed search engine for proteome-scale cross-link identification, running about 40 times faster than its predecessor. Proteomics researchers get answers in hours instead of weeks.
europmc-pmc6702459: Good health programs are designed, not improvised - but the design work is often invisible. Intervention Mapping is a step-by-step protocol for planning theory-based, evidence-backed health promotion, illustrated with real examples. The perspective piece shows planners how to move from good intentions to programs that actually work.
europmc-pmc6710759: Aging rusts us from within - oxygen's byproducts scar proteins and fats into compounds called ALEs and AGEs. This review traces how oxidative stress and these end products drive age-related decline. The chemistry of growing old, the authors argue, is largely the chemistry of slow burning.
europmc-pmc6711459: To map the brain's conversations, scientists model cause and effect between regions - that is Dynamic Causal Modelling. Part one of this guide covers first-level DCM analysis for fMRI: fitting the models to one person's data. The tutorial turns an intimidating method into a followable recipe.
europmc-pmc6744659: The m6A tag on RNA - a tiny methyl mark - behaves differently in every cancer. Surveying 33 cancer types, this study mapped how m6A regulators are altered and what that means for patients. The pan-cancer atlas turns a molecular detail into clinical insight.
europmc-pmc6770259: Curcumin promises much and delivers little - because the body barely absorbs it. This review tackles the bioavailability bottleneck: why the golden compound passes through unabsorbed and which formulations actually raise blood levels. The gap between hype and health, measured.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-59: This 2007 GAO report grades U.S. trade deals struck under fast-track rules — the process that lets the White House cut pacts Congress then votes up or down. GAO checks whether the deal-makers heard out Congress and private firms as the law demands. The report gives Congress a scorecard on talks that shape jobs and prices at home.
gao-gaoreports-b-299859: Alpha Genesis challenged a 2007 federal award, and GAO's ruling gives the final answer. The firm said the bid process was unfair; the call tests each claim and closes the book. For research and service firms in the government market, the verdict is another line in the fair-bidding code.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-559: Handshake deals were hiding in the Pentagon's books in 2007 — GAO's report says open-ended contract actions were undercounted and slow to get finalized. The findings expose the paperwork limbo where billions sat. The report demands that handshake buying get real contracts, and get them fast.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-759: Tank-killing tech needed a fair trial in 2007 — GAO's report dissects how the Pentagon judged active protection systems for armored vehicles. The findings grade the evaluation game. The report asks whether the best shield won, or just the best-connected bidder.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-259: Reserve troops' job rights needed better policing in 2007, and GAO's report says more action was required to oversee employment protections. The findings demand the enforcement. The report's cause: those who serve should not lose their jobs for it. The uniform should not cost a career.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-59: Medicare's medical-equipment bills were full of errors in 2007, and GAO's report says improvements were needed to curb the improper payments. The findings target the waste. The report warns that the wheelchair invoices needed a closer look. The program was paying for ghosts.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-159: The District's buying system was broken in 2007, and GAO's report says the procurement setup needed major reform. The findings demand the overhaul. The report warns that the capital's contracts deserved better than chaos. The city had to buy like it meant it.
openalex-w7205005059: Radishes are simple, but growing them well takes science. This agronomy study tested how different levels of shade affect radish growth in the soil and climate of western Amazonia. Conducted at the Federal University of Acre, the experiment measured which shade conditions produced the best crop. A small, concrete piece of agricultural research with direct value for farmers working under the Amazon sun.
openalex-w7205009059: Future science teachers learn their craft partly in real classrooms through Brazil's PIBID program. This study asks students in 7th and 8th grade what they thought of those trainee teachers and how well theory met practice in their science lessons. The authors measure the impact on learning and on the trainees' growth. A ground-level view of teacher training where the judges are the teenagers.
openalex-w7204461359: Government agencies need plans, not just reactions. This article studies the upsides of strategic planning in Brazil's indirect public administration, the state-run bodies that manage public interests. Based on descriptive research and literature review, the authors argue that structured planning serves the public mission better. A management study for readers who believe bureaucracy can be steered.
openalex-w7204463159: The Amazon holds a dazzling share of the world's orchids, and this study takes their census. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the orchid family in Amazonas state: species, endemics, hybrids, pollination, and conservation, using data current to mid-2026. A botanical overview as rich as its subject, and a baseline for protecting it.
openalex-w7204232059: Deepfakes poison the information well, and this paper proposes a defense. The authors present ETHOS-SE, a socio-technical framework for fighting AI-generated disinformation: part detection tech, part social design. They address the gap between lab advances and real-world trust. A forward-looking study of defending truth in the synthetic age.
openalex-w7204757659: Bones and teeth build themselves from calcium phosphate, and labs want to copy the trick. This review covers biomineralization-inspired routes to functional bioceramics. The authors surveyed how body-fluid chemistry guides the growth. A biomaterials review of nature's building code.
pmc-13470659: This 2026 review surveys dietary terpenoids — plant compounds found in herbs, fruits, and spices — for their role in blocking harmful biofilms in cancer prevention. The authors map the molecular chain of effects and how nano-sized delivery could help. It gathers a scattered field into one readable overview.
pmc-13456759: A 2026 case report of lung injury from e-cigarettes or vaping that appeared without the usual breathing symptoms, paired with a review of the literature. EVALI — vaping-associated lung injury — can be easy to miss when patients don't complain of shortness of breath. The paper alerts clinicians to look deeper when vapers present with other complaints.
pmc-13420959: This 2026 bioethics commentary argues that research priority-setting is not itself research — and calls for ethical clarity in Australia. When health services ask communities what to study, different ethical rules should apply. The paper draws a line the field has been blurring.
pmc-13418659: This 2026 neuroscience commentary discusses regional functional molecular profiles within the mammalian cortex, focusing on the limbic mesocortex — the transitional zone between emotion and cognition circuits. The author synthesizes molecular anatomy into a framework for understanding this in-between territory. It is expert-level brain cartography.
pmc-13639359: A 2026 paper on implementing colonoscopy quality at a health system level — Ontario's quality strategy. System-wide quality programs are hard to build. The pragmatic approach offers a template.
pmc-13632159: This 2026 multicenter study (PROMPT-LIPID) drew lessons from scaling a lipid-lowering clinical decision support intervention across US health systems. What works in one hospital may fail in ten. The lessons learned guide future rollouts.
pmc-13559359: A 2026 study predicting postoperative pulmonary infection after video-assisted thoracoscopic lung resection using an interpretable machine learning model. Interpretability matters for clinical trust. The model gives surgeons a usable risk tool.
pmc-13470259: A 2026 bibliometric analysis of virtual patients in medical education, based on Web of Science and Scopus databases. The publication trends map a growing field. The analysis shows where virtual patient research is heading.
pmc-13431459: In this 2026 Beijing cross-sectional study, women's knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding oral short-acting contraceptives after induced abortion were surveyed. Post-abortion contraception prevents repeat unintended pregnancy. The KAP data guide counseling.
pmc-13535259: This 2026 molecular biology paper showed the histone chaperone Spt6 regulates Set2, the enzyme that methylates histone H3 at lysine 36. The chaperone-enzyme relationship controls how chromatin is marked during transcription. The regulation is the mechanistic finding.
pmc-13511159: A 2026 andrology paper on the interplay between sperm function and seminal plasma biochemical profile in normozoospermic subjects. Even normal sperm counts hide variation. The interplay is the insight.
pmc-13509559: This 2026 optimization paper introduced a multi-strategy secretary bird algorithm for aesthetic color and layout optimization in visual art design. The nature-inspired optimizer served art. The algorithm is the novelty.
pmc-13506159: In this 2026 mixed-methods RCT, a visualization training platform improved PICU nurses' pain assessment skills in critically ill children. The training worked. The platform is the intervention.
pmc-13505959: This 2026 microbiology ode celebrated the 16S rRNA gene — its history, importance, caveats, and future in microbiome research. The marker gene got its tribute. The ode is both history and forecast.
pmc-13494559: In this 2026 molecular biology paper, AID self-assembly and multistranded DNA binding drove synapsis in class switch recombination. The antibody-diversifying enzyme's mechanism was detailed. The synapsis is the insight.
pmc-13487459: A 2026 mixed-methods study of nursing students' evaluation of a team-based clinical learning environment and mentoring. The students judged the model. The evaluation informs education.
pmc-13598559: In this 2026 paper, a targeted lipidomics workflow was developed for high-throughput phenotyping and mechanism-based in vitro hepatotoxicity studies. The lipid profiling served drug safety. The workflow is the tool.
pmc-13466359: In this 2026 review, cardiolipin as a signaling hub was examined — evolutionary conservation and programmable platforms coupling mitochondrial stress to cell fate. The mitochondrial lipid's signaling was synthesized. The hub framing is the insight.
pmc-13467959: A 2026 barley paper: heat and drought co-stress during microgametogenesis altered pollen development, fertility, and grain production in two-rowed winter barley. The combined stress hit reproduction. The altering is the agronomic warning.
pmc-13427759: This 2026 computational biology paper refined sequence-to-activity models by increasing model resolution. The sharper models predicted better. The refining is the advance.
pmc-13427059: This 2026 scoping review with translational framework examined quantitative electroencephalography in hemodialysis. The dialysis brain's electrical signals were surveyed. The framework bridges to practice.
pmc-13513159: A 2026 global review of chikungunya virus mosquito vectors — field surveillance and laboratory vector competence from 2020 to 2026. The vectors were cataloged. The review informs outbreak preparedness.
pmc-13463559: A 2026 case study developing InDel-based identification methods for wild and domesticated populations of the large yellow croaker. The fish's origins were genetically fingerprinted. The methods serve aquaculture.
pmc-13504959: In this 2026 paper, recurrent laryngeal nerve injury animal models were established using intraoperative neural monitoring in Sprague-Dawley rats. The voice nerve injury was modeled. The models serve thyroid surgery research.
arxiv-2606-15959: Scientists often replace slow physics simulations with fast neural networks, but the training data can be huge, so compression helps. Lossy compression, however, throws away detail. This paper measures how much that data loss hurts the neural network's accuracy. The authors map the tradeoff so labs can shrink their datasets without losing the quality they need.
arxiv-2606-16059: Financial institutions are hungry for faster, cheaper AI. This paper presents Mojo, a programming language and toolchain, as a promising route to scalable, efficient financial AI — work aimed at the practice section of Communications of the ACM. It argues Mojo's speed and simplicity make it well suited to the heavy numerical workloads of modern finance.
arxiv-2606-16259: Most stuff eases to rest on a set clock — yet glassy stuff drags far past it. This paper proves such drag for the triangle-chip game (a toy magnet board), in any head-count of dims. For slow-physics fans who clock glassy crawl.
arxiv-2606-16659: Scammers text fake links that lead to phishing webpages. FraudSMSWalker is a benchmark testing whether agentic large language models can trace an SMS scam to its webpage and detect the fraud. It gives security researchers a standard test for AI agents fighting mobile phishing.
arxiv-2606-16859: Molecules absorb light and dance in excited states — simulating that dance is costly. This paper makes machine learning of excited-state dynamics transferable across molecules, using 'extremal pooling.' It is for computational chemists. Learn once, dance many. One model, many molecules.
